inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 14 'Stock-based compensation cost' $213M (FY2024 $223M, FY2023 $219M); FY2022 10-K Note: $219M/$214M/$218M for FY2022/21/20. HAL does not itemise SBC on the cash-flow statement and does not disclose cash paid for net-share-settlement taxes separately (it sits inside 'Other' financing), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = the Note 14 cost. Not the equity-statement 'Stock plans' line, which nets option-exercise proceeds.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $1,007M (FY2024 $1,005M, FY2023 $800M); H1-2026 $308M. A genuine repurchaser: the flat count is funded, the diluted count fell 902M (FY2023) -> 838M (Q2 2026). Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (SBC expensed, count held flat).
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares (basic 836M + ~2M dilutive awards = 838M). Cover-page count 833.1M at 2026-07-17 after further buybacks; 838M is the latest dilutive-securities table figure and is held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2 2026 10-Q: long-term debt $7,071M + current portion $90M = $7,161M total debt; cash and equivalents $2,048M; net debt $5,113M. Operating lease liabilities ($287M current + $751M non-current = $1,038M) are EXCLUDED from net debt because operating-lease cost (~$394M FY2025) is already expensed inside operating income / EBITDA under ASC 842 (treatment B).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC of 9.0%: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 = ~10.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (FY2025 interest paid $432M on ~$7.2B) -> ~4.7% after 22% tax; weights ~79% equity (~$27B market cap) / ~21% debt. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality and commodity-price risk are charged ONCE, in the probability-weighted driver paths, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. ASC 842 operating-lease expense is inside EBITDA (no add-back), so lease liabilities are excluded from net debt and no separate lease_cost_pct_path is charged. D&A used for cash-tax EBIT is the reported DD&A line, which already excludes operating-lease ROU amortisation.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest ($42M at 2026-06-30; NCI share of net income $9M in FY2025) deducted once, in the equity bridge; flows are left whole.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical'), built per owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md on a MID-CYCLE basis. Halliburton is an oilfield-services cyclical: revenue tracks E&P capex, rig and completions activity and therefore oil prices, which are outside its control. Historical adjusted EBITDA margins (ex impairments/restructuring) ran 15.1% (FY2019) / 17.7% (FY2021) / 19.8% (FY2022) / 22.1% (FY2023) / 21.9% (FY2024) / 19.1% (FY2025, ex $831M charges) / ~17.6% (H1-2026 ex a $95M restructuring reversal). The base case therefore does NOT extrapolate the FY2023-24 peak (22%) or the current trough: it starts FY2026 at 18.0% (management guides sequential Q3 margin gains) and settles at a 19.5% mid-cycle level, below the five-year adjusted average of ~20%. FY0 = FY2025 (last full year, revenue $22,184M); FY2026 is year 1 and is modelled flat on H1-2026 revenue +1.7% YoY with Q3 guided down 2-5% sequentially (C&P flat to -2%, D&E -3 to -5%). Capex year 1 = management's ~$1.1B FY2026 guide (5.0% of revenue), then 5.5% mid-cycle (FY2023-25: 6.0/6.3/5.7%). D&A 5.2-5.3% (FY2025 5.1%, Q2-26 run-rate 5.2%). Cash tax 22% on EBIT (FY2024 ETR 22.2%, FY2023 20.8%; FY2025's 27% and H1-2026's 18.7% are both distorted by valuation-allowance moves). SBC ~0.95% of revenue, flat in dollars for six years. Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue change): receivables + inventory (~$8.2B) exceed payables (~$2.9B), so growth consumes cash. SAP S4 upgrade expense ($154M FY2025) is treated as a real operating cost inside the margin path. Terminal multiple capped at 13x owner FCF (cyclical, per the method's 12-15x guidance) against a 2.5% Gordon growth. Interest income ($88M FY2025) is NOT stripped: HAL is a net-debt company and the forward flows are unlevered, so it never enters the projection. Reported FCF ($1,672M FY2025) is the company's levered OCF - capex; last_fcf is that figure less SBC, retained for auditability only - the forward build is component-based and unlevered.

equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet; NCI charged once here, flows left whole

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (16.0%) is >30% above revenue 5yr CAGR (9.0%) and EPS 3yr CAGR is negative (-4.6%): FY2020 book value ($4,983M) sat at the bottom of $3.8B of impairments, so the equity CAGR measures a rebound from a written-down base, not compounding capacity. EPS 5yr is undefined (FY2020 loss of -$3.35/share). The 3yr revenue CAGR (FY2022 -> FY2025, mid-cycle to mid-cycle, 3.0%) is used as the through-cycle anchor for a cyclical.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs from the Metrics CSV (FY2020/FY2022/FY2025). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC: FY2020 $935M, FY2022 $1,012M, FY2023 $1,860M, FY2024 $2,200M, FY2025 $1,459M) versus reported 10.8%/7.7%; owner-FCF CAGRs are slightly HIGHER than reported because SBC has been flat in dollars ($213-223M) while FCF grew, so no rising share of growth is being paid in stock. EPS 3yr uses attributable net income / diluted shares (FY2022 $1.73 -> FY2025 $1.50). All three FCF endpoints are cycle-dependent: FY2025 carried $831M of impairments and other charges (~$300M cash severance) and FY2022 was early-upcycle, so none of these is a forward growth rate.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle: FY2026 flat, FY2027 +2% (management's 'softer than previously expected' short-to-medium term), then 3-4% tracking a ~5% industry CAGR net of North America share erosion; EBITDA margin 18.0% -> 19.5% mid-cycle.

bull.narrative: International/offshore upcycle plus a North America recovery from FY2027; margins return to the FY2023-24 22% level on Halliburton 4.0 mix and cost-out; capex rises with activity.

bear.narrative: Oil-price downcycle: revenue -8%/-4% in FY2027-28 (an FY2019-20-shaped but shallower contraction), margins trough at 14.5% (FY2019 underlying 15%), recover only to 17%; SBC and D&A sticky in dollars over a smaller base; capex cut then rebuilt.

scenario_narratives.base: Halliburton's revenue is a function of E&P capital budgets, which follow oil and gas prices with a lag; the company controls its cost base, technology mix (Halliburton 4.0 digital/AI, Sikal closed-loop drilling) and capital intensity, not its demand. The base case takes management at its word that the market is softer than expected over the short-to-medium term: FY2026 revenue flat (H1 +1.7% YoY, Q3 guided down 2-5% sequentially), FY2027 +2%, then 3-4% as international/offshore (decade-high $3.4B in Q2 2026 despite Middle East disruption) outgrows a structurally eroding North America land business. EBITDA margin starts at 18.0% (H1-2026 ~17.6% underlying, sequential improvement guided) and settles at a 19.5% mid-cycle, deliberately below the FY2023-24 peak of ~22% and the five-year adjusted average of ~20%. Capex follows the $1.1B FY2026 guide then 5.5% of revenue; working capital consumes cash on growth; SBC is small and flat. Terminal value capped at 13x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are (1) an international and deepwater capex upcycle in the Middle East, Latin America (Argentina, Brazil) and West Africa that runs several years, (2) a North America land recovery once oil stabilises above $70-75 and E&P consolidation runs its course, and (3) technology-led pricing on Halliburton 4.0 and integrated drilling that lifts EBITDA margins back to the 22% achieved in FY2023-24. Revenue compounds 6-7% for three years then decelerates; capex rises to 6% of revenue to fund the growth, so the FCF conversion improvement is mostly margin. Cap 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are (1) a sustained oil-price downcycle (OPEC+ supply additions, demand uncertainty) that cuts E&P budgets 10-15% and takes revenue down 8% and 4% in FY2027-28, (2) North America pressure-pumping overcapacity pushing pricing below cost recovery, (3) the Middle East disruption that is already dragging D&E becoming prolonged, and (4) negative operating leverage against a $7.2B debt stack, so margins trough at 14.5% (FY2019 underlying ~15%) and recover only to 17% as workforce cuts of 20-40% in affected divisions become permanent capacity loss. D&A and SBC are sticky in dollars over a smaller base; capex is cut to 4.5% then rebuilt. Cap 12x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the demand driver (oil price) is exogenous and management has itself flagged a softer market plus 20-40% workforce cuts; Brent fell >10% in 2025. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right at once - an international upcycle AND a North America recovery - while the international engine is already being disrupted in the Middle East. Base 50%. Risk is charged here, in the weights and driver paths, not in the discount rate.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a commodity-exposed oilfield-services cyclical. Value is anchored on a through-cycle 19.5% EBITDA margin and 3% revenue growth rather than on the FY2023-24 peak or the FY2025-26 trough; SBC is expensed and the diluted count held flat; leases are treated as operating cost; NCI deducted once; terminal value capped at 12-14x owner FCF because no buyer pays a compounder multiple for an oil-service franchise. The valuation is sensitive above all to the mid-cycle margin assumption (each 1pp of EBITDA margin is roughly $2-3/share) and to the terminal cap.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin: if 17% (bear) rather than 19.5% is the true through-cycle level, base value falls by roughly a quarter
Oil-price path: a 2019-20-style downcycle produces a bear case where FCF barely covers the dividend for two years and net debt/EBITDA rises above 2x
North America land is ~40% of revenue and structurally shrinking on E&P consolidation and efficiency gains; the base assumes international growth more than offsets it
Terminal value is 45-55% of EV under the 13x cap; the cap, not Gordon growth, binds, so the value depends on the exit multiple judgement
Balance-sheet vintage: net debt and shares are from the 2026-06-30 10-Q; Q3 2026 results (late October) will refresh both and the FY2026 guidance year
Unlevered cash tax at 22% of EBIT is above the 14-15% cash-taxes-paid/EBIT ratio of FY2023-25; if that gap persists the model is conservative by ~$0.5/share per point
